summary_paragraph: A woman with primary sclerosing cholangitis and Child-Pugh class B cirrhosis was admitted for acute epigastric and right upper quadrant abdominal pain radiating to the back, associated with low-grade fever and nausea. Imaging showed stable cirrhosis, portal hypertension, and retained biliary stones without evidence of acute pancreatitis or cholangitis. A single blood culture grew coagulase-negative staph, interpreted as a contaminant; vancomycin was briefly administered and discontinued. Hypoxia noted in the ED resolved and was attributed to opioid use. Her pain improved with conservative management, and she was discharged home on her baseline medications with instructions to monitor for recurrent symptoms and follow up for transplant evaluation and repeat EGD.
problems: Major depressive disorder, single episode, unspecified
